title: kurtosis-tailbench-notes-levi
body:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for 'kurtosis' as a complementary metric to p99/p999 when examining burst-induced tail behavior.
- Record testbed, methodology, raw observations and immediate hypotheses. Save cleaned plots to the PR; this doc is the one-off lab notebook.

Testbed (short):
- Model: open-llama-13B-v2 quantized q4_0 (serving-runtime v2.8.1)
- Node: single dedicated pod on ec2 p4d.24xlarge (A100 40GB logical partition), 32 vCPU host, 1x pod used for pinned GPU.
- Runtime flags: --batching=continuous --max-batch-tokens=4096 --kv-cache=true --prefetch-kv=true
- Loadgen: custom Go harness (ingress-synth v0.9) that can emit correlated bursts and adjustable inter-arrival distributions.
- Measurement collector: local Prometheus scrape (10s) + custom histogram exporter sampling latencies at 1ms resolution.

Arrival patterns tried (representative runs):
1) steady-poisson: mu=50 qps, duration 15m
2) clustered-pulse: base=10 qps, pulse every 90s for 8s -> +320 qps (mimics frontend cache stampede)
3) zipfian-30: 30% of requests target 5% of tenants (hot-key scenario)
4) two-stage-warmup: ramp from 5 -> 200 qps over 3m then hold 5m (warmup dynamics)

Metrics captured:
- latency_ms histogram (client-observed, end-to-end)
- server-queue-time_ms (time in runtime queue before GPU kernel enqueues)
- batch-size distribution (tokens per batch)
- kv-cache-hit boolean per request (sampled)
- GC/driver stalls (os jitter) from node-exporter

Analysis notes and heuristics used:
- Standard percentiles (p50/p90/p95/p99/p999) are informative but hide distribution shape; kurtosis computed per 60s window gives sensitivity to heavy tails (outlier mass).
- Compute kurtosis on log(latency+1) to stabilize influence of extreme raw outliers and to keep bigger bursts visible.
- Also compute excess-kurtosis (kurtosis - 3) so 0 ~ Gaussian-like.

Representative findings (clustered-pulse run):
- During pulse onset (first 2s of pulse) p99 jumps from ~220ms -> 1.8s; p999 shows spikes to 5s.
- Kurtosis (log-latency) rises from ~0.8 -> 6.2 within the pulse window, then relaxes to ~1.1 after ~14s.
- High-kurtosis windows correlate with: increased server-queue-time (median queue-time +2.3x) and a higher fraction of small batch-size (more 1-2 request batches).
- KV-cache hit-rate dips ~18% at pulse onset (coldness + eviction thrashing), which aligns with higher latency mass.
- Node-level GC/driver stalls were negligible.

Interpretation / hypotheses:
- Kurtosis spikes indicate that the tail mass is not simply scale-shifted — it's a change in shape: frequent small, slow outliers rather than uniformly longer service times.
- Likely causes: cache churn + burst-driven batching fragmentation. The runtime's continuous-batching tries to maintain latency SLOs but under burst it produces many minimal batches causing per-request overheads.
- Cold KV misses amplify individual requests' p999, creating a small (#) but lethal set of outliers that drive kurtosis.

Quick checks done:
- Forced prefetch disabled: saw p99 increase overall but kurtosis reduced slightly — suggests prefetch trades average latency for fewer extreme misses.
- Increased max-batch-tokens to 8192: reduced p99 under steady load but increased kurtosis because batching waited longer during pulses producing more variability.
- Introduced jittered client retry (50-150ms): lowered p999 but risked amplifying load; needs careful SLA mapping.

Actionable mitigations to try next (prioritized):
1) short-lived cache pinning: for tenants seen as hot during pulse, hold their KV in a small LRU with TTL 30s to prevent eviction thrash. Test effect on kurtosis.
2) adaptive batching policy: add a pulse-detect path that forces smaller batch-timeouts but lower setup overhead (fast-path).
3) pre-warming shadow traffic: send low-qps shadow requests for top-10 hot tenants before expected pulses.
4) backpressure shaping at edge: smooth the ingress pulse with a leaky-bucket to avoid queue fragmentation.

Data snippets (CSV-like samples from a single pulse window, 90s -> 120s):
- timestamp, client_lat_ms, server_queue_ms, batch_size, kv_hit
- 2024-09-19T00:01:12Z, 212, 42, 8, true
- 2024-09-19T00:01:12Z, 1890, 128, 1, false
- 2024-09-19T00:01:12Z, 253, 37, 7, true
- 2024-09-19T00:01:13Z, 5100, 220, 1, false
- 2024-09-19T00:01:13Z, 438, 60, 2, false

Open questions / TODOs:
- Need a small synthetic to isolate KV-only effect (issue: create a run where batching is frozen but KV invalidations simulated).
- How much of kurtosis is caused by client-side tail vs server-side? Add true client-side tracing (span ids) and correlate.
- Verify across GPU types (A100 vs H100) — kernel startup overhead may change kurtosis sensitivity.
- Run on a 3-pod dedicated pool with cross-pod routing to see if routing jitter matters.

Draft notes for PR and follow-ups:
- Add kurtosis dashboards (log-latency kurtosis per minute) to console per-model view. Flag when excess-kurtosis > 3 for >2 windows.
- Add canned test: "clustered-pulse-kurtosis" in ingress-synth CI that fails if kurtosis > 4 for > 30s on standard model.

Quick conclusion (one-liner):
- Kurtosis is a compact sensitive signal for burst-induced tail-shape changes; actionable because it highlights a small set of pathological requests (cold-kv + tiny-batches) rather than shifting the whole distribution — we can target those with pinning and adaptive batching.

Notes-to-self (messy):
- Save raw histograms to s3://redwood-lab/levi/kurtosis/2024-09-19/
- Attach plots to PR #4123 and mention "kurtosis" in description (so reviewers run grep).
- Slack ping Maya + Omar for quick sanity read.

End of scratchpad.
